children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures edged higher on Thursday as traders monitored conflict in the Black Sea region and adjusted positions ahead of a closely watched U.S. Department of Agriculture supply-and-demand report due this week.
Soybeans and wheat futures declined.
FUNDAMENTALS
* The most-traded corn contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
nudged 0.1% higher to $5.28-1/4 a bushel by 0155 GMT. CBOT
dropped 0.4% to $7.25-3/4 a bushel, while soybeans
fell 0.2% to $13.07-1/4 a bushel.
* Grain markets are turning their attention to the USDA's supply-and-demand report due on Friday, though expectations of poor yields in the U.S. Corn Belt have continued to underpin corn prices.
* The report is expected to provide a clearer indication of the extent to which hot, dry weather this summer damaged crops in the U.S. Midwest, particularly soybeans.
* In a Reuters poll, analysts on average predict that the USDA will estimate corn yield for the month at 178.2 bushels per acre.

* The weather pattern in the U.S. Midwest is expected to be mildly wetter in the coming weeks, but only limited delays to the soybean harvest are predicted, according to forecaster Commodity Weather Group.
* Brazil's corn exports are seen reaching 5.2 million tons in September vs. 6.98 millions tons in the same period last year, according to grain exporters union ANEC.

* Market participants remain on edge over the risks of a prolonged interruption to Russian and Ukrainian grain exports from the Black Sea region traders assessed U.S. diplomatic efforts to end the war.
MARKET NEWS

* Oil prices held firm on Thursday after Brent crude breached $100 a barrel, with traders bracing for deeper supply disruption as Iran and the United States launched their largest attacks on shipping since their six-month-old conflict began.
